prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat moire bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states at the magic angle

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a textbook case of a quantitative prediction followed by an experimental confirmation. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model (2011) located the flat bands at a specific twist angle, and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle showed the prediction was right. Independent groups have since reproduced the correlated states, and the physics has spread to twisted TMDs, fractional Chern insulators and other moire platforms. It is also a case where experiment overturned what theorists believed: nobody expected a purely carbon-based, weakly spin-orbit-coupled system to host this physics. The theory-plus-experiment pairing gives a clean, defensible three-person structure, and the discovery has changed how condensed-matter physicists think about tunable quantum matter. Because it ties calculation to measurement so tightly, it is the candidate on which I can best judge robustness myself.
statement.case_against: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled, so the interpretation is not fully stable, and the field is young enough that the committee could reasonably want a few more years of consolidation. Early sample-to-sample variability, and the 2018 reproducibility concerns, were real. The most serious attribution problem is on the experimental side: Yuan Cao, as first author, is not among the credited names. The wider moire platform (Dean, Kim, Yacoby and others) also has claims, so any three-name allocation will look arbitrary to some. If the committee judges recognition premature, a more mature candidate such as optical lattice clocks is the obvious fallback.

responses.point: Pearce ranks B043 second and B029 only sixth. He sees the twisted-graphene discovery as exceptional in impact, but is concerned that Yuan Cao is not among the credited names, that the superconducting mechanism is unsettled, and that it may be a little early.
responses.response: I take the Cao point seriously, and it is the strongest attribution objection to B029. But the Nobel record has long credited the group leader who conceived and directed the experiment, and the 2018 papers came from Jarillo-Herrero's group; a student's role does not by itself decide the allocation. The unsettled pairing mechanism does not undermine the central discovery. The existence of flat-band correlated phases at the magic angle is robust and reproduced by many groups, and that is what a citation would honour. On timing I accept a degree of earliness, but I do not think 'mechanism unknown' has disqualified earlier superconductivity prizes. I would phrase the citation around the flat bands and correlated states, not around the pairing mechanism.

responses.point: Lindroth places optical lattice clocks (B043) first as a mature, clean, two-person case: Katori's magic-wavelength idea realised and brought to 1e-18 by Ye, in a natural line after the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
responses.response: I agree that B043 is the more mature and the better-attributed candidate, and I ranked it lower mainly because it lies outside my field and I defer to you and Kroll on atomic physics. Where I hesitate is whether it reads as a distinct discovery rather than a continuation of the precision-timekeeping line already honoured in 2005 and 2012. I would like to hear whether you see the redefinition of the second as a condition for the prize. If the committee wants a safe, well-attributed choice this year, I would not oppose B043 and keep it as my first alternative. I would still argue that B029 reveals new quantum behaviour in matter, which I give more weight.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks the dislocation-mediated melting and hexatic phase (B020) first as a clean, universal mechanism with decades of confirmation, arguing recognition is overdue. He also ranks B029 third as a new paradigm with a clean theory-plus-experiment pairing.
responses.response: We agree on B029's structure, and I welcome that. On B020 I accept the physics is elegant and that decades of colloidal and simulation work support it. But I see two difficulties: the experimental picture is system-dependent (first-order in some systems, two-step in others), which weakens the claim of a single verified discovery, and the 2016 prize on topological defects already covers much of the intellectual ground. I would want to see evidence that the hexatic phase is observed in a form that settles the theory before I rank it above B029. I do not think B020 should be dismissed, but I do not see it as more robust than the moire result.

responses.point: Kroll gives B043 first place because the magic-wavelength idea is simple and original, and the record of 1e-18 uncertainties and international comparisons shows maturity. He places B029 outside his ranking.
responses.response: I agree on the physics of B043 and the independent confirmation across Sr, Yb and Hg. Our disagreement is about what we prefer to reward: a precision measurement tool, or a new state of matter. Both are legitimate. I would ask you how you weigh the fact that B029 shows quantum mechanics producing a state nobody predicted in that form, against a metrology advance whose headline consequence, the redefinition of the second, has not yet happened. I do not claim your view is wrong, only that it is not obvious that the clocks must outrank the moire discovery.

uncertainties: How the committee will resolve the experimental attribution in twisted bilayer graphene, in particular the roles of Yuan Cao and the other 2018 co-authors.
Whether the superconducting pairing mechanism needs to be understood before a prize, or whether the flat-band correlated phases are a sufficient discovery.
Whether the redefinition of the second is a prerequisite for optical lattice clocks, which would affect the timing of B043.
I rely on memory for dates and priority details and have not verified them against the literature.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I am a theoretical condensed-matter physicist at Uppsala, and the profile lists no collaboration with MacDonald, Bistritzer or Jarillo-Herrero, but my field is close to B029 and I note that proximity as a possible bias.
